KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.claim: Abraham identifies all gods worshipped instead of God as fabricated and their worshippers as misguided; God alone creates, guides, feeds, gives drink, heals, causes death and life, and forgives sins on Judgment Day.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r4.anchor: gerçek ve tapılmaya lâyık olan tanrının yaratan, hidayete erdiren, yediren, içiren, şifa veren, öldüren, hayat veren ve kıyamet gününde günahları bağışlayan Allah Teâlâ olduğuna dikkat çekmiştir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r6.claim: God’s creation and guidance of Abraham are undeniable realities and a logical necessity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r6.anchor: The fact that God created him and guided him is an undeniable reality and also a logical necessity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r7.claim: God gave human beings abilities, a noble nature, and intellect that distinguishes right from wrong and develops and uses those abilities; Islahi connects this with the Qur’anic account of creation and guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r7.anchor: He has created them with a noble nature and blessed them with intellect which can distinguish right from wrong.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r1.claim: Guidance necessarily follows from God’s act of creation: leaving people to wander would contradict His mercy and wisdom and make creation futile and unjust.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r1.anchor: The God Who has created human beings with all these provisions and with such wisdom cannot leave them to wander about.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r2.claim: Since human intellect alone cannot secure their highest attainable status, God supplies their spiritual needs through prophets and messengers as well as their material needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r2.anchor: He in fact instituted a system of divine guidance by sending His prophets and messengers to mankind.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r3.claim: Only the source of all blessings deserves worship, not stone idols that cannot hear or see and can neither benefit nor harm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r3.anchor: only that being is worthy of worship who is the fountainhead of all these blessings and favours

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.claim: Abraham presents the fundamentals of his preaching in logical order as personal impressions rather than argument, because in the acquittal and migration phase intellectual persuasion is useless; the subtle style may still stir hearts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.anchor: instead of presenting them through arguments and reasoning, he has expressed them in the form of personal impressions.

BURSEVI:v6p205/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205/r1.claim: The phrase 'who created me' describes the Lord of the worlds, who brought Abraham from nonbeing into being.
BURSEVI:v6p205/r1.anchor: {الذى خلقنى} (از عدم بوجود آورد) صفة رب العالمين

BURSEVI:v6p205/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205/r2.claim: God alone guides Abraham to the welfare of both abodes through guidance beginning with creation and the continuing gift of spirit; the fāʾ and present tense indicate its ongoing renewal.
BURSEVI:v6p205/r2.anchor: {فهو} وحده {يهدين} يرشدني إلى صلاح الدارين بهدايته المتصلة من الخلق ونفخ الروح متجدد على الاستمرار

BURSEVI:v6p205/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205/r3.claim: Guidance begins with the fetus being directed to absorb blood in the womb and culminates in guidance to the path of Paradise and its delights.
BURSEVI:v6p205/r3.anchor: وذلك أن مبدأ الهداية بالنسبة إلى الإنسان هداية الجنين إلى امتصاص دم الحيض من الرحم ومنتهاها الهداية إلى طريق الجنة والتنعم بلذائذها

BURSEVI:v6p205/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205/r4.claim: The wording points to abandoning reliance on causes and acquisition in prophethood, sainthood, and intimacy with God: these are gifts rooted in primordial election, though their gradual appearance can mislead the veiled into thinking they were earned.
BURSEVI:v6p205/r4.anchor: بل أشار إلى الاصطفاء الأزلي وذلك أن جميع المقامات اختصاصية عطائية غير نسبية حاصلة للعين الثابتة

BURSEVI:v6p205/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p205/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p205/r5.claim: The author's cited couplet contrasts people who strive for union with those who entrust it to fixed divine decree.
BURSEVI:v6p205/r5.anchor: قال الحافظ : قومي بجهد وجد نهادند وصل دوست

QIRAAT-ER:26:78:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:78:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:26:78:2#1/r1.claim: The variant restores the explicit first-person yāʾ after khalaqanī, fully vocalizing the pronoun suffix.

QIRAAT-ER:26:78:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:78:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:26:78:5#1/r1.claim: The variant keeps the full yāʾ on the first-person object suffix after yahdī, extending its vowel.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r9.claim: الذي خلقني can be accusative as an adjective of رب العالمين or with an implied أعني, or nominative as the predicate of an omitted هو.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r9.anchor: وأجازوا في الذي خلقني النصب على الصفة لرب العالمين، أو بإضمار، أعني: والرفع خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي هو الذي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r10.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r10.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses الذي as a subject and فهو يهدين as its predicate, with فاء because the clause has a conditional sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r10.anchor: وقال الحوفي: ويجوز أن يكون الذي خلقني رفعا بالابتداء، فهو يهدين: ابتداء وخبر في موضع الخبر عن الذي، ودخلت الفاء لما في الكلام من معنى الشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r11.claim: The author rejects that parsing: الذي is specific rather than general, and خلق cannot describe an ongoing condition relative to Abraham; an extra فاء would also be unacceptable here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r11.anchor: وليس الذي هنا فيه معنى اسم الشرط لأنه خاص، ولا يتخيل فيه العموم، فليس نظير: الذي يأتيني فله درهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r12.claim: يهدين is glossed either as guiding Abraham to obedience or to Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r12.anchor: بقدرته فهو يهدين إلى طاعته. وقيل: إلى جنته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes continuous guidance beginning once creation is complete, including guidance to nourishment in the womb, finding the breast, and suckling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p164/r13.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فهو يهدين، يريد أنه حين أتم خلقه، ونفخ فيه الروح عقب هدايته المتصلة التي لا تنقطع إلى ما يصلحه ويعينه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq retains the first-person yāʾ in يهديني and the following verbs; this is also reported from Nāfiʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r8.anchor: وأثبت ابن أبي إسحاق ياء المتكلم في يهديني وما بعده، وهي رواية عن نافع.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r1.claim: The relative clause describes the Lord; naming creation and the following attributes clarifies His lordship for guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r1.anchor: ( الذي خلقني ( صفة لرب العالمين ووصفه تعالى بذلك وبما عطف عليه مع اندراج الكل تحت ربوبيته تعالى للعالمين زيادة في الايضاح في مقام الارشاد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r2.claim: Alternatively, these are specified blessings to Abraham, detailed because they especially warrant worshipping God alone and relying on Him for benefits and protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r2.anchor: وقيل : تصريحا بالنعم الخاصة به عليه السلام وتفصيلا لها لكونها أدخل في اقتضاء تخصيص العبادة به تعالى وقصر الالتجاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r3.claim: He alone guides Abraham to what is beneficial and right in worldly and afterlife matters, with guidance continuing from creation through his lifetime.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r3.anchor: فهو يهديني وحده جل شأنه إلى كل ما يهمي ويصلحني من أمور المعاش والمعاد هداية متصلة بحين الخلق له هداية متدرجة من مبتدأ إيجاده إلى منتهى أجله

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r4.claim: This guidance enables Abraham, by nature or choice, to gain benefits and avert harms; human guidance begins with fetal nourishment and ends with guidance to Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r4.anchor: مبدؤها بالنسبة إلى الانسان هداية الجنين لامتصاص دم الطمث في المشهور ومنهاها الهداية إلى طريق الجنة والتنعم بنعيمها المقيم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r5.speaker: الحوفي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r5.claim: They parse the relative pronoun as the subject and هو يهديني as its predicate; the predicate takes فاء because the relative phrase implies a condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r5.anchor: وجوز الحوفي وغيره كون الموصول مبتدأ وجملة ( هو يهديني ) خبره ودخلت الفاء في خبره لتضمنه معنى الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that this construction needs a general relative antecedent, which this one lacks; creation also cannot newly occur for Abraham.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r6.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بأن الفاء انما يؤتى بها في خبر الموصول لتضمنه معنى الشرط اذا كان عاما

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r7.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r7.claim: The construction might be explained by al-Akhfash's allowance for adding فاء to a predicate without a conditional implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r7.anchor: فلعل ذلك على مذهب الأخفش من جواز زيادة الفاء في الخبر مطلقا نحو زيد فاضربه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r8.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r8.claim: The response says generality is not a strict requirement for this فاء, but only the usual case.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r8.anchor: وأجيب بأن اشتراط العموم غير مسلم كما فصله الرى وإنما هو أغلبي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r9.claim: A second response says creation can recur in the abstract and be intended here, and that creation causes guidance through divine wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r9.anchor: وبأن مطلق الخلق مما يمكن فيه التجدد وهو ممكن الارادة وإن ظهر في صورة المخصوص وتسبب الخلق للهداية بمقتضى الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r10.claim: The proposal that creation merely grounds the statement of already-existing guidance is dismissed.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p95/r10.anchor: وقيل : إنه سبب للاخبار بها لتحققها وليس بشيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p117#2/r5.claim: God created Abraham and guides him to the path of salvation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r2.claim: God guides every creature to the purpose for which it was created in worldly and afterlife affairs, as in the verse about the One who determined and guided.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r2.anchor: لأنه يهدي كل مخلوق لما خلق له من أمور المعاش والمعاد كما قال تعالى والذى قدر فهدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r3.claim: Guidance develops from creation to life's end, enabling benefits and warding off harms; for humans it begins with the fetus drawing menstrual blood in the womb and ends in guidance to Paradise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r3.anchor: هداية مدرجة من مبدأ إيجاده إلى منتهى أجله يتمكن بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r4.claim: The ف in فهو is causal if the relative clause is the predicate, but conjunctive if it modifies Lord of the worlds, since creation is completed while guidance continues.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:77-79/r4.anchor: والفاء للسببية إن جعل الموصول مبتدأ وللعطف إن جعل صفة رب العالمين فيكون اختلاف النظم لتقدم الخلق واستمرار الهداية

SULAMI:v2p75#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r1.claim: When intimacy with God overwhelmed Abraham, he avoided naming the Beloved directly and spoke by attribute; early in attraction, before such absorption, he called out to his Lord.
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : لما استغرق بهم في الخلة احتشم من ذكر خليله بالتصريح

SULAMI:v2p75#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r2.claim: God created me for servanthood and guides me toward nearness to Him.
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : الذي خلقني لعبوديته يهديني إلى قربه

SULAMI:v2p75#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r3.claim: The One who enslaved and employed me made this easy and guides me toward what pleases Him in me.
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين : الذي استعبدني واستخدمني سهل على ذلك وتهديه إلى ما يرضيه عني

SULAMI:v2p75#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r4.claim: God created me to summon His creatures and will guide me to the manners of intimacy with Him.
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : الذي خلقني لدعوة خلقه سيهديني إلى آداب خلته

SULAMI:v2p75#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r5.claim: Junayd says God created things outwardly through other things, but reserved the heart's bond with Him for Himself, as His treasury and the locus of His secret on earth.
SULAMI:v2p75#2/r5.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : إن الله خلق الأشياء في الظاهر بالأشياء ما خلا القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r11.claim: Because God alone created Abraham, only He can know a creature's inward state and control it completely; He has every perfection and can benefit or harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r11.anchor: لأنه لا يعلم باطن المخلوق ويقدر على كمال التصرف فيه غير خالقه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r12.claim: The human being has a bodily form from the realm of creation and a spiritual form from the realm of command; bodily formation comes first.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r12.anchor: والإنسان له قالب من عالم الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r13.claim: Creation is expressed in the past because it does not recur in this world, while guidance is present-tense because it recurs in religious and worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r13.anchor: وذكر الخلق بالماضي لأنه لا يتجدد في الدنيا

TUSTARI:26:78/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:26:78/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:26:78/r1.claim: God created Abraham for servitude and guides him toward nearness to Him.
TUSTARI:26:78/r1.anchor: الذي خلقني لعبوديته يهديني إلى قربه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#4/r1.claim: Qatada reports the saying that God's first blessing on a servant is creating him.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : الذي خلقني فهو يهدين قال : كان يقال اول نعمة الله على عبده حين خلقه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq's account says Abraham's mother fled to a cave in labor; Abraham declared that his creator, provider, feeder, and giver of drink was his sole Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2779#5/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق ، فلما وجدت أم إبراهيم الطلق خرجت ليلا إلى مغارة فذكر القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r1.claim: The relative clause most likely describes رب العالمين, and فهو يهدين continues its relative clause: as creator, God alone is most entitled to govern what He created.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r1.anchor: الأظهر أن الموصول في موضع نعت ل { رب العالمين } ( الشعراء : 77 ) وأن { فهو يهدين } عطف على الصلة مفرع عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r2.claim: Alternatively, الذي begins an independent nominal sentence and فهو يهدين is its predicate, with فاء added because the relative resembles a conditional.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الموصول مبتدأ مستأنفا به ويكون { فهو يهدين } خبرا عن { الذي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r3.claim: Either parsing links God’s creation of Ibrahim to his exclusive devotion, like Ibrahim’s turning toward the One who originated the heavens and earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r3.anchor: وعلى الاحتمالين ففي الموصولية إيماء إلى وجه بناء الخبر وهو الاستدراك بالاستثناء الذي في قوله : { إلا رب العالمين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r4.claim: Fronting هو before the verbal predicate restricts guidance to God, overturning the claim that idols control it; it is not a pronoun of separation after a conjunction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r4.anchor: لتخصيصه بأنه متولي الهداية دون غيره لأن المقام لإبطال اعتقادهم تصرف أصنامهم بالقصر الإضافي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r5.claim: The present tense يهدين conveys guidance as a continuing, renewed act.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r5.anchor: والتعبير بالمضارع في قوله : { يهدين } لأن الهداية متجددة له .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r6.claim: The فاء makes guidance follow creation because guidance arises from the intellect God created, as in the verse saying He gave each thing its form and then guided it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r6.anchor: وجعل فعل الهداية مفرعا بالفاء على فعل الخلق لأنه معاقب له لأن الهداية بهذا المعنى من مقتضى الخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r7.claim: Here guidance means showing paths to knowledge, including shielding reason from false suggestions so reflection can avoid error; the author compares it to showing the two paths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p142/r7.anchor: والمراد بالهداية الدلالة على طرق العلم كما في قوله تعالى : { وهديناه النجدين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun rather than coordinating all clauses directly emphasizes the possessor of these three magnificent divine attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.anchor: وتكرير اسم الموصول في المواضع الثلاثة مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن تعطف الصلتان على الصلة الأولى للاهتمام بصاحب تلك الصلات الثلاث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r9.claim: By naming actions in the sensible world that are evident to everyone, Ibrahim’s descriptions of God aim to lead the idolaters to faith if they seek guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r9.anchor: وقد أشار في هذه النعوت إلى ما هو من تصرفات الله في العالم الحسي بحيث لا يخفى عن أحد قصدا لاقتصاص إيمان المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.claim: The five divine acts span bodily and intellectual creation, food and water, illness and healing, death, and resurrection; together they trace physical life and the second life as gifts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.anchor: فذكر خلق الجسد وخلق العقل وإعطاء ما به بقاء المخلوق وهو الغذاء والماء ، وما يعتري المرء من اختلال المزاج وشفائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.claim: These descriptions also prepare for spiritual perfection: death looks like a blessing only after reflection, while the life after it is plainly a blessing for whoever wills it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.anchor: وذكر الموت الذي هو خاتمة الحياة الأولى ، وأعقبه بذكر الحياة الثانية للإشارة إلى أن الموت حالة لا يظهر كونها نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.claim: The first-person yāʾ is omitted from four verbs for lightness and rhyme at pauses, since most endings in this surah use a still nūn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.anchor: وحذفت ياآت المتكلم من { يهدين ، ويسقين ، ويشفين ، ويحيين } لأجل التخفيف ورعاية الفاصلة لأنها يوقف عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.claim: Abraham lists divine actions that warrant divinity, including actions relevant to humans, so people can understand their Lord; this is courteous phrasing, and all comes from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.anchor: أتى إبراهيم عليه السلام في هذه الأوصاف التي وصف الله عز وجل بها بالصفات التي المتصف بها يستحق الألوهية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129/r1.claim: God guides Abraham to right guidance, unlike the things his people worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129/r1.anchor: أي إلى الرشد لا ما تعبدون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.claim: Abraham argues that divinity belongs only to the one who performs these acts of creation, guidance, provision, healing, and forgiveness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.anchor: وهذا احتجاج على قومه أنه لا تصلح الإلهية إلا لمن فعل هذه الأفعال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r1.claim: God created and determined the creatures' course, guiding them to it; He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r1.anchor: هو الخالق الذي قدر قدرا، وهدى الخلائق إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r2.claim: God alone guides some and leads others astray as He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p146/r2.anchor: وهو الذي يهدي من يشاء ويضل من يشاء.

JISHUMI:v7p5366/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r10.claim: God's creation of Abraham is followed by guidance because guidance completes all blessings.

JISHUMI:v7p5366/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r11.claim: Guidance can mean directing Abraham to the path of goodness.

JISHUMI:v7p5366/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r12.claim: Another interpretation is guidance to Paradise: God charges Abraham with worship here and guides him to Paradise hereafter.
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r12.anchor: إلى الجنة، كلفني في الدنيا بعبادته ويهديني في الآخرة إلى جنته

JISHUMI:v7p5366/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r13.claim: Guidance can also mean that God supports Abraham through His gracious aid.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r1.claim: One explanation is that God created Abraham by grace and guides him to obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r1.anchor: الي خلقني بنعمته فهو يهدين لطاعته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God created Abraham for worship and guides him to Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r2.anchor: الثاني : الذي خلقني لطاعته فهو يهديني لجنته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r3.claim: Although creation and guidance describe all people, Abraham cites them to prove obedience: a benefactor must be obeyed, and others should follow his commitment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r3.anchor: إنما ذكرها احتجاجا على وجوب الطاعة , لأن من أنعم وجب أن يطاع ولا يعصى

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r8.claim: Abraham identifies the Creator as the one who guides him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r1.claim: God created Abraham in the secure womb and guides him to worldly paths and the interests of religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r1.anchor: بالتكوين فى القرار المكين ﴿ فهو يهدين ﴾ لمناهج الدنيا ولمصالح الدين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r2.claim: The future tense after creation may imply that God will guide him to what is most necessary, best, and most complete.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r2.anchor: والاستقبال فى يهدينى مع سبق العناية لأنه يحتمل يهدينى للاهم الأفضل والأتم الأكمل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that God created Abraham for His service and guides him to the manners of intimacy with Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#11/r3.anchor: أو الذى خلقنى لأسباب خدمته فهو يهدينى إلى آداب خلته

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r1.claim: God guides Abraham to religion and provides his food and drink.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r1.anchor: أي يرشدني إلى الدين. { والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين } أي يرزقني.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r6.claim: The final ya is omitted in these verse endings to make the rhyme agree; Ibn Abi Ishaq instead reads the forms with ya.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r6.anchor: وكله بغير ياء: { يهدين } { يشفين } لأن الحذف في رؤوس الآي حسن لتتفق كلها.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r7.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq reads all these forms with ya, since ya is a pronoun and the nun was added for a reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق على جلالته ومحله من العربية هذه كلها بالياء لأن الياء اسم وإنما دخلت النون لعلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r8.claim: Abraham cites these blessings to establish the duty to obey the benefactor and not disobey him.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r8.anchor: إنما ذكرها احتجاجا على وجوب الطاعة لأن من أنعم وجب أن يطاع ولا يعصى

RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.claim: Abraham’s attribution of guidance to God here, in 26:78, and in his prayer of 14:35 clearly establishes the author’s theological position.

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r1.claim: After mentioning the Lord of the worlds, Abraham describes God by qualities that make him worthy of worship; the passage announces four qualities and begins with creation and guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r1.anchor: ما وصفه به مما يستحق العبادة لأجله ، ثم حكى عنه ما سأله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r2.claim: Creation and guidance together provide all benefits to every being capable of receiving benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r2.anchor: الخلق والهداية بهما يحصل جميع المنافع لكل من يصح الانتفاع عليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r3.claim: Some say the human belongs to the bodily realm of creation; others say the spiritual realm of command. The body’s formation precedes the heart’s reception of spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r3.anchor: فمنهم من قال هو من عالم الخلق والجسمانيات ، ومن قال هو من عالم الأمر الروحانيات

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r4.claim: Razi reads ‘when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit’ as bodily composition followed by the divine luminous subtlety from the realm of command.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r4.anchor: فالتسوية إشارة إلى تعديل المزاج وتركيب الأمشاج ، ونفخ الروح إشارة إلى اللطيفة الربانية النورانية

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r5.claim: The verses about the human’s clay origin and later bodily stages point to the spirit from the angelic realm; guidance comes through the spirit, showing creation precedes guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r5.anchor: وذلك إشارة إلى الروح الذي هو من عالم الملائكة ، ولا شك أن الهداية إنما تحصل من الروح

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r6.claim: Razi links God’s praise as creator and guide here to the same pairing in the opening verses of al-Aʿlā.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أنه سبحانه أثنى على نفسه بهذين الأمرين في قوله : { الذى خلق فسوى * والذى قدر فهدى }

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r1.claim: Human embodiment develops from semen mixed with menstrual blood, both deriving from food made from the four elements; their hot, cold, moist, and dry qualities interact into a balanced temperament ready for governing powers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r1.anchor: بدن الإنسان إنما يتولد عند امتزاج المني بدم الطمث

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r2.claim: Plant powers attract, retain, digest, and expel food, replace what is lost, grow the organs, and leave surplus material for reproduction.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r2.anchor: قوى نباتية وهي التي تجذب الغذاء ، ثم تمسكه ثم تهضمه ثم تدفع الفضلة المؤذية

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r3.claim: Animal powers include perception through the senses, imagination, memory, and recollection, plus active powers such as appetite and anger and the forces operating in the muscles.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r3.anchor: قوى حيوانية بعضها مدركة كالحواس الخمس والخيال والحفظ والذكر

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r4.claim: Human powers are intellectual and practical; the intellectual powers apprehend realities in spiritual and bodily, higher and lower realms.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r4.anchor: ومنها قوى إنسانية وهي إما مدركة أو عاملة ، والقوى المدركة هي القوى القوية على إدراك حقائق الأشياء الروحانية والجسمانية

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r5.claim: Every component of the bodily world has things that suit and complete it and things that oppose and harm it, along with powers that attract the fitting and repel the harmful; well-being therefore requires creation and guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r5.anchor: وجدت لها أشياء تلائمها وتكمل حالها وأشياء تنافرها وتفسد حالها

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r6.claim: Creation means bringing the person into existence, while guidance means the powers that draw benefits and repel harms, so the phrase gathers worldly and religious benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r6.anchor: أما الخلق فبتصييره موجودا بعد أن كان معدوما

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r7.claim: Creation is phrased in the past because the self is created once, whereas guidance is phrased in the present because divine direction recurs continually through worldly and religious benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r7.anchor: أما هدايته تعالى فهي مما يتكرر كل حين وأوان

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r8.claim: Worldly guidance lets the senses distinguish benefit from harm; religious guidance lets reason distinguish truth from falsehood and good from evil at every moment.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r8.anchor: وذلك بأن تحكم الحواس بتمييز المنافع عن المضار

RAZI-FULL:v24p127#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p127#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p127#2/r6.claim: Abraham did not restrict himself to praise while teaching people the true religion: he rejected their gods, praised God, then prayed; a preacher must teach the religious practice.
RAZI-FULL:v24p127#2/r6.anchor: ثم ذكر الثناء ، ثم ذكر الدعاء لأن الشارع لا بد له من تعليم الشرع

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.claim: Only a being capable of the listed acts is worthy of worship.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.anchor: Only a being capable of the acts listed in these verses is worthy and deserving of worship

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.claim: Symbolically, God nourishes the soul, heals its ailments, and enlivens the spirit by bringing death to the passionate ego.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.anchor: Interpreted symbolically, these verses can mean that God feeds and nourishes the soul, heals the ailments of the soul, and enlivens the spirit

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.speaker: Al-Thaʿlabī
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī describes spiritual death and life as justice and grace, disobedience and obedience, separation and meeting God, and ignorance and knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.anchor: Al-Thaʿlabī summarizes the spiritual dimensions of these verses by saying that God brings death through justice and life through grace

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.claim: Others say people die outwardly yet live inwardly, die through forgetting God, and live through remembering Him.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.anchor: one is caused to die outwardly, but is given life inwardly, dies through forgetfulness of God, and lives through remembrance of Him (Su)

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.speaker: Junayd
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.claim: Junayd compares resurrection to nakedness, hunger, and thirst, except for those clothed in reverence and given gnosis and love.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.anchor: Some quote Junayd, who says that when human beings are resurrected on the Day of Judgment

TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r1.claim: God guides Abraham to sound speech and action and directs him to right guidance.
TAB-FULL:v17p591#2/r1.anchor: {الذي خلقني فهو يهدين} [الشعراء: 78] للصواب من القول والعمل، ويسددني للرشاد

SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r1.claim: Alladhī can be an adjective of rabb, an appositional substitute, an explanatory apposition, or accusative after an implicit verb meaning I mean.
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r1.anchor: يجوز فيه أوجه: النصب على النعت ل " رب العالمين " أو البدل، أو عطف البيان، أو على إضمار أعني.

SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r2.claim: Alladhī can instead be nominative as the predicate of an implicit subject, or as a subject itself.
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r2.anchor: والرفع على خبر ابتداء مضمر أي: هو الذي خلقني أو على الابتداء.

SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r3.claim: Fa-huwa yahdīn is a nominal clause serving as the predicate of alladhī.
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r3.anchor: و[قوله]: { فهو يهدين } جملة اسمية في محل رفع خبرا له.

SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r4.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r4.claim: Al-Ḥawfī says the fa appears because the subject contains conditional meaning; the author rejects this because the relative has a specific referent and its clause is not renewed.
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r4.anchor: قال الحوفي: " ودخلت الفاء لما تضمنه المبتدأ من معنى الشرط ". وهذا مردود؛ لأن الموصول معين ليس عاما

SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ follows al-Ḥawfī, though he does not discuss the fa; the author's objection applies if his rationale is the same.
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r5.anchor: وتابع أبو البقاء الحوفي ولكنه لم يتعرض للفاء. فإن عنى ما عناه الحوفي فقد تقدم ما فيه.

SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r6.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r6.claim: If Abu al-Baqāʾ instead follows al-Akhfash, this would allow an extra fa in predicate position generally, as in Zayd fa-ḍribhu.
SAMIN-DURR:26:78/r6.anchor: تابعا للأخفش في تجويزه زيادة الفاء في الخبر مطلقا نحو: " زيد فاضربه "

TABATABAI:26:74-78/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r7.claim: Against the view that “who created me” begins an insignificant new passage, the author argues that Abraham begins with creation to infer that God also governs his affairs.
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r7.anchor: استيناف من الكلام لا يعبأ به.

TABATABAI:26:74-78/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r8.claim: In gradual bodily existence, creation and governance cannot be separated; because God creates, he also manages, and the fāʾ in “then guides me” makes guidance follow from creation.
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r8.anchor: لوضوح أن الخلق والتدبير لا ينفكان في هذه الموجودات الجسمانية التدريجية الوجود

TABATABAI:26:74-78/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r9.claim: The unqualified “guides me” means guidance to all beneficial ends, worldly or otherworldly; its present tense conveys ongoing guidance from creation onward and forever.
TABATABAI:26:74-78/r9.anchor: أن المراد به مطلق الهداية إلى المنافع دنيوية كانت أو أخرويه

TABATABAI:26:79-81/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r1.claim: The guidance given after creation can mean universal direction to each creature's benefits, as in Moses's description of God, and echoes the surah's sign in the growth of plants.
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r1.anchor: ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى طه 50، أي هداه إلى منافعه وهي الهداية العامة

TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.claim: On the universal reading, feeding, drinking, and healing are particular instances of general guidance; if guidance means religious guidance, these qualities stand separately and guidance precedes other gifts as the best blessing after existence.
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r2.anchor: من الصفات المعدودة من قبيل ذكر الخاص بعد العام

TABRISI:26:78-84/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r2.claim: God brought Abraham from nonexistence into being and guides him toward what will save him.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r2.anchor: وأخرجني من العدم إلى الوجود { فهو يهدين } أي يرشدني إلى ما فيه نجاتي

TABRISI:26:78-84/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:26:78-84/r3.claim: An alternative is that God created Abraham for obedience and guides him to Paradise.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r3.anchor: وقيل: الذي خلقني لطاعته فهو يهديني إلى جنته

TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.claim: The final yāʾ letters are omitted because these are verse endings.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.anchor: وإنما حذف الياءات لأنه رؤوس الآيات

TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.claim: Abraham's speech argues against his people that only the one who performs these acts deserves divinity.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.anchor: وهذا الكلام من إبراهيم ع إنما صدر على وجه الاحتجاج على قومه والإخبار بأنه لا يصلح للإلهية إلا من فعل هذه الأفعال.

THALABI:v7p166/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p166/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p166/r9.claim: Abraham says the true guide is the creator; there is no guide besides Him.
THALABI:v7p166/r9.anchor: أخبر أن الهادي على الحقيقة هو الخالق لا هادي غيره

THALABI:v7p166/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p166/r10.speaker: أهل اللسان
THALABI:v7p166/r10.claim: The people of language say God created Abraham in the world upon his innate nature and guides him in the afterlife to His Garden.
THALABI:v7p166/r10.anchor: قال أهل اللسان: الذي خلقني في الدنيا على فطرته فهو يهدين في الآخرة إلى جنته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “He guides me” as “He directs me.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says God guides Abraham to religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r2.anchor: وقال # الكلبي: فهو يهدين إلى الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r3.claim: God alone guides to religion and right direction, not the idols, because Abraham's opponents claimed their gods guided them; the creator is the guide.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى: فهو الذي يهدين إلى الدين، والرشد، لا ما تعبدون من الأصنام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r4.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the fāʾ, rather than wāw, connects the guidance clause as a response or consequence of the preceding creation clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p68#2/r4.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: وجاءت الفاء دون الواو في (فهو) لأن الفاء تجعل ما بعدها متصلا بما قبلها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r3.claim: The one who created Abraham is the one who guides him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r3.anchor: قال: {الذي خلقني فهو يهدين} [الشعراء: 78] الذي خلقني وهداني.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r9.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq retains the first-person yā in يهديني and the following verbs; this is also transmitted from Nafi.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r9.anchor: وأثبت ابن أبي إسحاق ياء المتكلم في ( يهديني ) وما بعده وهي رواية عن نافع

DURR-FULL:v6p305/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r6.claim: Qatāda says the first blessing God gives a servant is creating him.
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كان يقال أول نعمة الله على عبده حين خلقه

DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet promises guidance, Paradise food and drink, healing and expiation, blessed life and martyrdom, forgiveness, wisdom, truthful renown, and Paradise homes for one who recites Abraham’s prayer after ablution while leaving for obligatory prayer; al-Ḥasan adds a prayer for the parents.
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا توضأ العبد لصلاة مكتوبة فاسبغ الوضوء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r6.claim: After creating Ibrahim and breathing life into him, God continuously guides him toward what benefits him, including nourishment and the skills of infancy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323#2/r6.anchor: فهو يهدين } يريد أنه حين أتم خلقه ونفخ فيه الروح ، عقب ذلك هدايته المتصلة

BURHAN:v4p68/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p68/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p68/r3.claim: Abraham uses the past for completed creation and the present for continuing guidance; fa makes guidance an answer to the creative act and marks God's exclusive guidance against the idolaters' claim that their gods guide them.
BURHAN:v4p68/r3.anchor: اتى بالماضي في خلق لان خلقه مفروغ منه واتى بالفاء دون الواو لانه كالجواب

ITQAN:v2p579/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p579/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p579/r1.claim: Past-tense verbs indicate an occurrence; present-tense verbs indicate an action that recurs. Al-Zamakhshari states this about God’s mocking the hypocrites.
ITQAN:v2p579/r1.anchor: المراد بالتجدد في الماضي الحصول وفي المضارع أن من شأنه أن يتكرر ويقع مرة بعد أخرى صرح بذلك جماعة منهم الزمخشري

ITQAN:v2p579/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p579/r2.speaker: بهاء الدين السبكي
ITQAN:v2p579/r2.claim: Al-Subki explains that saying God knew something in the past locates the statement in past time without implying that God’s knowledge began then; the wording can describe an eternally continuous attribute.
ITQAN:v2p579/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ بهاء الدين السبكي وبهذا يتضح الجواب عما يورد من نحو علم الله كذا فإن علم الله لا يتجدد

ITQAN:v2p579/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p579/r3.speaker: بهاء الدين السبكي
ITQAN:v2p579/r3.claim: In Abraham’s wording, creation is past because it is completed, while guidance, feeding, giving drink, and healing use the present for recurring acts.
ITQAN:v2p579/r3.anchor: فأتى بالماضي في الخلق لأنه مفروغ منه وبالمضارع في الهداية والإطعام والإسقاء والشفاء

ITQAN:v3p293/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.claim: Al-Tibi says Abraham’s speech combines a graceful transition and a good request: he moves from God’s attributes to “My Lord, grant me judgment and join me with the righteous.”
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.anchor: قال الطيبي ومما اجتمع فيه حسن التخلص والمطلب معا قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

ITQAN:v3p240/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.claim: Al-Tafwit is presenting varied meanings, such as praise and description, in separate sentences of equal measure; it may use long, medium, or short sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.anchor: هو إتيان المتكلم بمعان شتى من المدح والوصف وغير ذلك من الفنون كل فن في جملة منفصلة

ITQAN:v3p240/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.claim: Abraham's successive statements about God's guidance, provision, healing, death, and revival exemplify al-tafwit in long sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.anchor: فمن الطويلة ﴿ الذي خلقني فهو يهدين والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

ITQAN:v3p240/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r4.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p240/r4.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isbaʿ says the Qur'an has no al-tafwit example composed of short sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r4.anchor: قال ابن أبي الاصبع ولم يأت المركب من القصيرة في القرآن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.claim: Abraham attributes creation, guidance, food, drink, and healing to God, but says ‘when I am ill’ rather than ascribing illness to God.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r6.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه نسب الخير إلى ربه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.claim: In Abraham's account, fa links creation to guidance without delay, while thumma marks resurrection as delayed after death.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.anchor: فقد عطف في الآية الأولى بالفاء لتعقب بلا مهلة الهداية للخلق

NASHR:v2p336/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p336/r10.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p336/r10.claim: Yaqub affirms the sixteen listed extra yāʾs in both connected and pause forms: the eight quoted forms plus أطيعون in eight places.
NASHR:v2p336/r10.anchor: أثبت الياء في جميعها يعقوب في الحالين
